classification.difficultyReason: Reduce fourth powers to a cosine model, solve a periodic inequality within the five-minute window, and distinguish that window from the proportion over a complete period.

content.prompt:
The power output $P$, in kilowatts, is modelled by

$$P(t)=120(\sin^4t+\cos^4t),$$

where $t$ is time (minutes) after the turbine begins operating. The trigonometric arguments are measured in radians.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 45, between the shared model and part (a)

children.label: b
children.prompt: The turbine operates at high efficiency when the power output is at least $105\text{ kW}$. State the values of $t$, in the first five-minute window, for which the power output is at a high efficiency.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
90+30\cos4t&\ge105\\
30\cos4t&\ge15\\
\cos4t&\ge\frac12
\end{align*}$$

The trigonometric arguments are in radians. For each integer $k$,

$$\begin{align*}
-\frac\pi3+2k\pi&\le4t\le\frac\pi3+2k\pi\\
-\frac\pi{12}+\frac{k\pi}{2}&\le t\le\frac\pi{12}+\frac{k\pi}{2}
\end{align*}$$

Restricting to $0\le t\le5$ gives

$$\begin{aligned}
t\in{}&\left[0,\frac\pi{12}\right]\cup\left[\frac{5\pi}{12},\frac{7\pi}{12}\right]\\
&{}\cup\left[\frac{11\pi}{12},\frac{13\pi}{12}\right]\cup\left[\frac{17\pi}{12},\frac{19\pi}{12}\right]
\end{aligned}$$

where $t$ is in minutes. All endpoints are included because the threshold is “at least” $105\text{ kW}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: For what proportion of the time is the turbine operating at high efficiency?

answer.short:
$\frac13$.

High efficiency occupies one third of each complete period.
answer.worked:
The period of $\cos4t$ is $\frac\pi2$ minutes. In $0\le t\le\frac\pi2$, high efficiency occurs on $\left[0,\frac\pi{12}\right]$ and $\left[\frac{5\pi}{12},\frac\pi2\right]$.

$$\begin{align*}
\text{High-efficiency duration}&=\frac\pi{12}+\left(\frac\pi2-\frac{5\pi}{12}\right)\\
\text{High-efficiency duration}&=\frac\pi6\text{ minutes}\\
\text{Proportion}&=\frac{\pi/6}{\pi/2}\\
\text{Proportion}&=\frac13
\end{align*}$$
